## Comparability Caveat

These two fiscal years are **not directly comparable on an as-originally-reported basis**. On November 3, 2021, IBM completed the spinoff of its managed infrastructure services unit into Kyndryl Holdings, Inc., and "the historical results of Kyndryl have been presented as discontinued operations in these consolidated financial statements" [DOC-3]. As a result:

- FY2020 revenue **as originally reported** in the FY2020 10-K was **$73,620 million**, which included the managed infrastructure business [DOC-1].
- FY2020 revenue **as recast** for continuing operations in the FY2022 10-K was **$55,179 million** [DOC-2].
- FY2022 revenue was **$60,530 million**, reflecting continuing operations only [DOC-2].

Comparing the FY2022 figure against the original FY2020 figure would produce an apparent decline of roughly **–17.8%** ($60,530M vs. $73,620M) [DOC-1][DOC-2], but that difference is driven almost entirely by the Kyndryl separation, not by underlying business performance.

## Like-for-Like Calculation

Using the continuing-operations basis consistently (both figures as presented in the FY2022 10-K):

$60,530M − $55,179M = $5,351M
$5,351M ÷ $55,179M = **9.7%**

This is the economically meaningful growth rate over the two-year period (roughly 4.7% compounded annually).

ANSWER: Approximately +9.7% on a comparable continuing-operations basis ($55,179M in FY2020 to $60,530M in FY2022); the –17.8% figure derived from the originally reported FY2020 revenue of $73,620M is not comparable because of the Kyndryl spinoff.
